short: The largest naval battle of World War II, which effectively destroyed the Imperial Japanese Navy.
full:
From 23 to 26 October 1944, American and Australian forces clashed with the Imperial Japanese Navy near the Philippine islands of Leyte, Samar, and Luzon. The battle was triggered by the Allied invasion of Leyte, which aimed to cut off Japan from its vital supply lines of oil and rubber in Southeast Asia. For the first time, Japanese forces carried out organized kamikaze attacks, throwing everything they had into a desperate defense.

Despite heavy initial resistance, the Allied fleets decimated Japanese naval power. Japan lost four aircraft carriers, three battleships, and numerous cruisers and destroyers, a blow from which their navy never recovered. The victory paved the way for the liberation of the Philippines and left the Allies in complete command of the Pacific, severely isolating the Japanese home islands.
